title: What Does the Bible Say About Abortion? 25 Verses
description: What the Bible says about unborn life, the womb and the one passage that touches on harm to a pregnant woman, with the verses people on each side cite.
keywords: what does the bible say about abortion
is abortion a sin in the bible
bible verses about life in the womb
summary: The words abortion, fetus and embryo do not appear in the World English Bible or the King James Version (0 verses each), so Scripture never addresses abortion by name. People who see it as wrong point to passages that speak of God forming and knowing a person in the womb (Psalm 139:13-16, Jeremiah 1:5, Luke 1:41-44) and to the command not to murder (Exodus 20:13). The one legal text that involves a pregnant woman is Exodus 21:22-25, and readers split on whether it treats the unborn child as a life equal to the mother's, which is why Christian traditions disagree on its application. The word womb appears in 75 verses of the World English Bible. The verses below are the ones most often cited on every side of the question.

faqs.a: No. Neither the World English Bible nor the King James Version contains the word abortion, fetus or embryo. Churches that oppose abortion reason from verses about God's care for life before birth (Psalm 139:13-16, Jeremiah 1:5) and the command against murder (Exodus 20:13). Others point out that no verse addresses the question directly and read Exodus 21:22-25 differently.

It sets the penalty when men fighting hurt a pregnant woman. If she gives birth prematurely and no harm follows, the man pays a fine. If harm follows, the penalty is life for life, eye for eye. Readers differ on whether the harm is to the woman only or also to the child, and on whether 'gives birth prematurely' means a live birth or a miscarriage.

faqs.q: Does Psalm 139 prove life begins at conception?
faqs.a: Psalm 139:13-16 says God formed the psalmist's inward parts and wove him together in his mother's womb, and that God's eyes saw his unformed body. Many Christians read this as God's personal care for a person before birth. It is a poem about God's knowledge, not a statement about when personhood starts, and the verses do not mention conception.

faqs.q: What do Christian churches teach about abortion?
faqs.a: The Catholic Church and the Orthodox churches oppose abortion. Most evangelical denominations oppose it with varying exceptions, while some mainline Protestant bodies allow it in certain circumstances. This page lists the verses; it does not ask you to take a side.
